turns.content: Okay, so. Julian and I had this really nice chat about music after last month's club. He lent me a graphic novel. I had this dumb idea to slip a silly anonymous note in it before I give it back, but no. That's too much. I refuse to make the group weird. My actual question: I found a 3-track ambient synth link. Sharing it in the group Discord — casual or too pointed?

Sharing it in the group Discord sounds casual, especially if people already post music there. You enjoyed talking with Julian and want to keep the group comfortable; a music link doesn’t have to turn that into a big statement.

Keep it genuinely group-facing: “Found this little three-track ambient synth release—thought some of you might like it.” No need to tag Julian or refer back to your conversation.

My recommendation: post it in the music or off-topic channel if there is one, then let people respond—or not—without making his reaction the test of whether posting was okay.
Right, posted it. No tag. Good advice. He replied a few hours later with just a music emoji. That's a nothing response, right? Should I just leave it.

You kept it low-key, as you wanted. His emoji is a small acknowledgment—not enough to tell whether he’s interested, but not a rejection either.

I’d leave it there. An emoji doesn’t call for a reply, and you can still chat naturally next time you see him.

Right. I'll leave it. The note idea is dead, I know. But I keep thinking about the book he lent me. Any harm in just handing it back at the next meeting with a neutral "thanks"? Or does that feel like I'm overthinking it.

Yes—handing it back at the next meeting with a simple “thanks for lending me this” is completely ordinary. You’re trying to keep the group comfortable, but that doesn’t require being distant.

If you enjoyed it, you can say so; that’s not a loaded signal. My recommendation: return it, thank him, and let any conversation happen naturally.

Fair enough. Neutral thanks, no note, no emoji chase. Feels right. One more thing. The club is meeting at a bar next week. First time outside the library. Does that change anything or is it still just give the book back and let it sit.

Still give the book back and let it sit. Your low-key plan fits what you want.

The bar may make conversation more relaxed, but the venue change doesn’t tell you anything new about Julian’s interest. Say “thanks for lending me this,” and if you end up chatting, enjoy it—you don’t need to cut things short to stay neutral.

My recommendation: keep the return simple and treat the evening as a chance to enjoy the group, not a test of what’s happening with him.
Right. Book back, neutral thanks, let it sit. Bar changes nothing. Got it.
Sounds like a plan you’re comfortable with. Keep the book return simple, and enjoy the evening—you can be friendly without needing to figure out what it means.
